page.layout: One page of verse, one column of italic text. Running head at top centre, page number at top left. No margin notes. Catchword "Hic" at the lower right, below the last line.

l.i: Natus Pannonia Cæsar dictare solebat,
Conveniunt multi nebulones & Parasiti,
Unum ut decipiant nil prorsus tale verentem,
Securum, incautum: non restitit ipse duobus
Alcides, qui si tulerint quandoque repulsam, Non
ideo repetunt minus acres prælia, donec
Victus ad extremum dare tandem cogitur
arma. Tantum continuaq; preces repetitaq; verba
Saepius, inculcata diu, variasque per artes
Argumenta valent. quanto magis esse cavendum
Nobis, quorum obsessa tenet præcordia fallax,
Et blandus monitor, qui tot se vertit in ora,
Protea quot perhibent varias mutasse figuras
Præsto semper adest, & vellicat improbus aurem
Assidue, nec finem ullum facit ante monendi,
Quam specie utilium persuasit turpia nobis. Hic
Laertiadæ quondam persuasit Ulyssi,
Suspensam sterilis patriam de vertice saxi
Innumeris præferre bonis, vitaq; deorum.
Hic Paridem Phrygium Veneris postponere formæ
Virginis intactæ cælestia dona subegit,
Dedecus & probrum patriæ præferre saluti.
Hic tentare Iouis thalamos, aufumquè pudicam
Attrectare Deam, stuprúmque offerre maritæ
(Fecissétque etiam, nisi nubis falleret error)
Perdidit; & claros imitantem fulguris ignes
Nimborumq; sonos vero Salmonea telo.
Perculit, ac iustas exegit in Elide pœnas.

page.notes: Small printed marks stand at the start of lines 5 ("Alcides"), 11 ("Assidue") and 23 ("Attrectare"). They look like printer's pointing signs, not note references, so I left them out. "2IO" at the top left: the 0 is printed like an O, and I kept it as printed. "obsessa" in the line "Nobis, quorum obsessa tenet" is a little unclear in the scan but is the best reading. "Fecissétque" is also a little uncertain. Line-end hyphenation is absent on this page. Only the catchword "Hic" was found beyond the verse, at the lower right.
